teams.heading: Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi dies in Japan after suspected training heatstroke
teams.body: The Fijian rugby community is mourning the tragic passing of back-rower Saimoni Vunilagi, who died in Japan on Friday aged 26. Vunilagi, who recently joined second-division club Kyuden Voltex, was hospitalised after showing severe symptoms of heatstroke following a practice session last Monday in Fukuoka, where temperatures reached 35C. The 6ft 5in forward previously played for Tokyo Sungoliath. His devastated club released a statement saying: "We humbly pray for the repose of his soul and extend our heartfelt condolences to his bereaved family."

lead.why: The sudden and tragic death of Fijian forward Saimoni Vunilagi in Japan has shocked the rugby community and led today's coverage.

teams.heading: Joe Jenkins keeps Wales options open following Leicester Tigers switch
teams.body: Dual-qualified centre Joe Jenkins has admitted he is keeping an open mind about his international future following his summer move to Leicester Tigers. The 22-year-old, who left Bristol Bears after four years, is eligible for Wales through his father. While Jenkins represented England at under-20s level, former Wales age-grade coach Byron Hayward previously claimed the midfielder wanted to wear the red jersey. However, Jenkins insists his immediate focus remains on earning a starting spot with his new Premiership club.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi's makeshift Argentina side suffer narrow defeat to South Africa
teams.body: A makeshift Argentina line-up pushed world champions South Africa to the limit on Saturday, ultimately falling to a narrow 17-10 defeat in Buenos Aires. Despite missing suspended fly-half Tomás Albornoz and captain Julián Montoya, Los Pumas led early through a Benjamín Grondona try. An inexperienced front row featuring debutant Francisco Moreno and loosehead Boris Wenger excelled, while wings Rodrigo Isgro and Ignacio Mendy constantly threatened. However, South Africa's powerful bench eventually overwhelmed the hosts, denying Felipe Contepomi's side a famous victory.

teams.heading: Les Kiss guides Wallabies to tense debut victory over Japan
teams.body: Les Kiss began his tenure as Wallabies head coach with a gritty 35-32 victory over Japan in Osaka on Saturday. Despite playing in sweltering 32C heat and losing lock Miles Amatosero to a 20-minute red card just before half-time, Australia held off a fierce fightback. Tries from Harry Potter, Tom Wright, Max Jorgensen, Fraser McReight and Taniela Tupou secured the win. 'When we had to find a way, we did find a way,' Kiss said.

teams.heading: Warner Dearns scores late but Brave Blossoms fall to Australia
teams.body: Japan pushed Australia all the way in sweltering Osaka conditions on Saturday, ultimately falling to a 35-32 defeat. Despite the Wallabies playing with 14 men following Miles Amatosero's red card, the hosts struggled to capitalise, though they stayed in touch with tries from Ryunosuke Ito, Faulua Makisi, and Ueda. A late converted try from Warner Dearns in the 78th minute brought the Brave Blossoms within three points, but the visitors held on to deny Japan their first Test victory over the Wallabies.

teams.heading: Patrick Tuipulotu admits shock as Ma'a Nonu named for Sharks clash
teams.body: All Blacks lock Patrick Tuipulotu admitted surprise following the selection of 44-year-old legend Ma'a Nonu for Tuesday's tour match in Durban. Nonu, a double World Cup winner, was named on the Sharks bench to face his former side at Kings Park, a move Tuipulotu described as a spectacle for the game. Skipper Luke Jacobson leads a power-packed New Zealand side featuring Damian McKenzie and Jordie Barrett, as Dave Rennie's men look to build on Friday's 38-21 victory over the Stormers.

teams.heading: Rassie Erasmus recalls 39-year-old Deon Fourie for upcoming All Blacks series
teams.body: The Springboks have handed a shock recall to veteran utility forward Deon Fourie following his standout performance for the Stormers against New Zealand on Friday. Fourie, who turns 40 next month, was drafted into the squad after captain Siya Kolisi suffered a hamstring injury during Saturday’s 17-10 win over Argentina. While Erasmus confirmed the skipper’s setback "doesn't look too bad," the inclusion of "Brannas" provides experienced cover for a gruelling schedule. André Esterhuizen also remains a doubt following a late head injury assessment in Buenos Aires.
